epics.title: Stand up an EDD harness inside pm to prove SEMANTIC parity across supported platforms -- the gate that a structural test can never provide. Uses ~/Documents/Repos/edd-harness (the maintainer's public, open-source, domain-agnostic Python EDD library). What gets evaluated: the ancillary artifacts an AGENT interprets non-deterministically -- commands/*.md, skills/conductor/SKILL.md, agents/*.md, hook-injected output, and the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md rules block. Explicitly NOT scripts/conductor.mjs, which is deterministic and already covered by 250 unit tests. Key design insight: pm's agent behavior is already observable because the engine IS the instrumentation -- a correctly-followed instruction leaves deterministic traces (a MINIMAL line in detours.log, a correctly-laned epic in state.json, a refreshed rules block), so most scorers are deterministic check() calls rather than paid JudgeScorers, landing the corpus on edd-harness's BLOCKING gate rather than its advisory one. Scorers encode DESIRED behavior absolutely rather than diffing platforms against each other, because two platforms failing identically is parity but still broken; parity is therefore 'every supported platform passes the same corpus'. Lives in an in-repo evals/ dir alongside the other not-shipped tooling (.claude/skills/, docs/, openspec/) so an artifact and its scenario change in ONE commit -- a separate repo would recreate the very drift problem platform-parity-mechanism exists to solve. Design doc: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-edd-harness-agent-behavior-testing-design.md

rulesBlock() hardcodes Claude Code slash-command syntax (/pm:status, /pm:detour --minimal, /pm:resume) throughout the emitted CLAUDE.md rules text, plus the 'Manage with /pm:status · /pm:next · ...' footer. On any platform without slash commands, that text is actively misleading -- it instructs the agent to run commands that don't exist there. Needs a command-style notion so the block can emit the direct CLI form (node scripts/conductor.mjs render) instead. rulesBlock() already takes (tracker, reviewMode, secondaryTrackers) so an added parameter fits the existing signature. Prerequisite for any multi-platform support; found during the multi-platform-agent-support brainstorm.

Build the mechanism that keeps every supported platform at parity with the Claude Code base, BEFORE any second platform exists. Three layers, mirroring how this repo already enforces documentation currency: (1) MECHANICAL -- a machine-parseable parity ledger (one markdown file with a table, OpenSpec supported-tools.md style, parsed directly by a CI test so exemptions are real config not prose) plus a conductor.test.mjs gate that enumerates Claude Code artifacts (commands/*.md, hook events in hooks/hooks.json, skills/, agents/) and FAILS CI when any lacks either a per-platform counterpart or an explicit exemption row with a reason; generic over whatever platforms the ledger lists, so it passes trivially at zero platforms and starts enforcing the moment codex is added. (2) PROCEDURAL -- a project-local skill that walks each platform directory in order, reads what changed in the Claude Code base, determines the per-platform delta, applies it, and updates the ledger; same shape as release-checklist/mintlify-doc-sync. (3) Semantic parity is explicitly NOT this epic's job -- a structural test can prove a counterpart file exists but never that it behaves the same; that gap is closed by the edd-harness sibling epic. Deliberately sequenced before codex-platform-support so the gate never has a window where drift could start unobserved.

epics.title: Port pm to Hermes Agent (Nous Research) -- the FIRST non-Claude-Code platform, ahead of Codex, per maintainer preference (used more actively; CLI+GUI shape is a harder, more informative test of the architecture than Codex). Verified hands-on against Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20, git install at ~/.hermes/hermes-agent, docs vendored locally at website/docs/): hermes CLI exposes hooks/skills/plugins/mcp/project subcommands plus -z PROMPT for headless and --accept-hooks to bypass first-use consent. THREE hook systems exist; only SHELL HOOKS fit pm (CLI+Gateway, any language so Node is fine, can block AND inject context) -- Gateway hooks are gateway-only and Plugin hooks are Python-only. Shell hooks use a stdin/stdout JSON wire protocol with hook_event_name/tool_name/tool_input/session_id/cwd, and CRUCIALLY the docs state Claude-Code-style {decision:block,reason} is accepted and normalized internally. VALID_HOOKS includes pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, pre_llm_call, on_session_start/end/finalize/reset, subagent_start/stop, pre_verify. Mapping: gate-guard->pre_tool_call (direct), commit-nudge->post_tool_call (direct). TWO OPEN DESIGN PROBLEMS: (1) context injection appears bound to pre_llm_call which fires EVERY turn, not on_session_start, so the briefing would repeat unless the hook self-dedupes on session_id (available in the payload); (2) shell hooks are declared in user-level ~/.hermes/config.yaml rather than shipped in a plugin manifest, and Hermes plugin hooks are Python-only while pm's engine is Node -- so pm likely needs a thin Python shim shelling out to conductor.mjs, or an install step that writes config.yaml entries. Also no PreCompact equivalent found. Needs its own brainstorm before implementation. hermes plugins install takes a Git URL or owner/repo, same distribution model as Claude Code and Codex, so cfdude/pm can serve all three. Bonus: 'hermes hooks test <event>' fires hooks against a synthetic payload, which may let EDD test hook scenarios far cheaper than a full agent run.
